R.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: R1 supplies pixels and timestamps; R3 supplies the candidate interval used after extraction.
1. Hand pose is measured each processed position; face/body feature measurements occur every eighth position. A hand point needs confidence≥0.15; at least five usable hand points are required.
2. R2 point locations define hand boxes over R1 pixels (hand scale 1.70, union 1.20, minimum box fraction 0.14). Square RGB256×256 crops use reflected border padding and area/cubic resize. Image encoding caches 512 values per valid view, plus masks and normalized boxes.
3. For each candidate, trim active evidence, fill bounded gaps (hands≤3 positions; face/body≤16), and normalize XY by shoulder-centered scale, with wrist/palm fallback. Depth=log(reference apparent size/current size), not metric Z.
4. Landmarks use p=j(N−1)/31: linear x/y/depth/confidence, nearest presence. Hand features select 16 nearest cached times over the same trim.
OUTPUT TO R.b/R.c: [B,32,61,5], [B,16,3,512], [B,16,3], [B,16,3,4]. Presence distinguishes missing points from real zeros.
R.source: Source supplement: LiveReelCore.swift:151,616,679,756,789; LiveReelModels.swift:190,296. Paper input contract: printed p.76.

R.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: normalized landmark tensors from R.a. B counts candidate intervals.
1. Append masked first/second XYZ differences: five raw channels become 11 per node. These sampled-index differences are not meters/second.
2. Compute 33 selected within-hand pair distances per hand, masked by both endpoints' presence. Source uses the XYZ vector norm; Z is a relative scale proxy, not measured depth.
3. Per-time inputs: hand 264, hand 264, face 165, body 44. Each projects to 64 and passes through one regional temporal block. Concatenate four outputs →256.
4. Four global blocks process [B,32,256], with eight parallel heads per block and kernel 15. One block: half feed-forward residual → attention → depthwise temporal convolution → half feed-forward residual → normalization.
5. Q=XWq, K=XWk, V=XWv; learned projections create queries, keys and values. Attention=softmax(QKᵀ/√dₖ)V. Global heads each use 32 features (256/8), and scores span 32×32 time comparisons per head. Those two 32 s have different meanings. A global convolution expands 256→512, uses GLU→256, depthwise kernel 15, then a pointwise projection. Attention already supplies global context; kernel 15 is not a limit on the full model. Pool with learned masked time weights α: h=Σαₜhₜ →[B,256], then 100 logits.
OUTPUT TO R.c: pooled landmark embedding and logits. Four regional branches precede the four global blocks.
R.source: Source supplement: recognition/model_v17.py:masked_temporal_features, _pairwise, PartwiseTemporalEncoderV17, SqueezeformerBlockV17, _pool. Selected architecture metadata; paper §2.1.4.

R.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: appearance tensors/masks/boxes from R.a and landmark outputs from R.b.
1. Layer-normalize 512-dimensional crop features and project to 256. Project [four box coordinates+validity] to 256; add learned view identity.
2. Softmax over three view scores, mask missing views and renormalize. Weighted sum gives [B,16,256]; add learned time positions.
3. Three temporal blocks (width 256, heads 8, kernel 7) plus masked attention pooling give [B,256] and 100 hand logits.
4. Z-score each branch's 100 logits: z=(l−mean(l))/max(std(l),ε). Baseline=0.75 z_landmark+0.25 z_hand.
5. Concatenate normalized embeddings (512 values) and both score vectors (200): residual input 712 → hidden 384 → hidden 384 →100. A sigmoid gate from the 512 embedding values scales this correction.
OUTPUT TO R5: baseline+gated residual. Primary is retained by default; adapted fusion evidence is used only by guarded transition logic. Inference fixes learned parameters; attention weights still depend on the input.
R.source: Source supplement: model_hand_mobileclip2_v17.py; model_unified_multimodal_v17.py; export_dual_confidence.py; LiveReelModels.swift:312. Metadata verified from the selected checkpoint.

R.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: R2 observations supply timing features; R4 supplies each candidate's word scores. These are reused evidence streams.
1. Boundary features 450=122 XY+122 time-scaled motion+61 presence+61 confidence+84 hand-local. Window[1,64,450] plus mask[1,64] → O/B/I logits[1,3]. Six-position lookahead is nominally 0.30 s at 20 Hz; it is one delay component.
2. Candidate scores combine recognition, activity and beginning evidence. Current word settings: wR2, wA0.25, wB0.5, c−1.5, θ0.4; inner activity floor 0.5. S=2 max(log q,log θ)+0.25Σlog a+0.5 log b−c.
3. Search: best[t]=max(best[t−1]+rest, best[s]+S(s,t−1)); backtrack the compatible path. Commit policy adds lag 6, context 2 and guarded early acceptance. Nearby repeated-label handling is separate from search (word gap 20 positions); it can suppress an intended rapid repeat. Early commits need 3 stable updates, score≥0.9 and span≥4, with unsafe-label exclusions.
4. Accepted glosses/scores → paper T5 evidence tokens; encoder→decoder token loop. Finish flushes pending events before final English and local speech.
OUTPUT: committed gloss events, then final English/audio. T5 remains the paper path in this board.
R.source: Source supplement: LiveReelModels.swift:97–190; LiveReelDecoder.swift:58,405,700,820; LiveReelStage3.swift. Paper: pp. 78–82.

H.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: H1 camera frames, H2 extracted observations/appearance cache and H3 candidate intervals.
Keep the physical HELLO event separate from its sampled representation: the candidate duration can vary while the landmark input remains 32 times and the hand input 16 times.
TOY interpolation, one coordinate only (not a measured HELLO value):
1. Neighboring observed coordinate values are 2 and 6.
2. A target sample lies one quarter of the way between them: α=0.25.
3. Difference=6−2=4.
4. Interpolated value=2+0.25×4=3.
The real routine repeats this per continuous channel and joint. Presence uses nearest-neighbor selection; images are not made by averaging those coordinate numbers.
OUTPUT TO H4: fixed-shape evidence for each proposed interval, with validity information still attached.
H.source: Worked illustration; actual sampling implementation: LiveReelCore.swift:756 and LiveReelModels.swift:296. Same contracts as R.a.

H.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: H4 recognizer outputs for two intervals over the same event, plus H3 timing.
TOY confidence values only: A assigns HELLO0.80; B assigns HELLO0.90. In each 100-class distribution, the remaining mass belongs to the other 99 classes. These values are not measured ATLAS outputs.
1. A and B overlap, so accepting both as independent segments is incompatible with the non-overlapping path search.
2. Compare whole candidate sequences using boundary/activity evidence as well as class scores.
3. The larger HELLO probability alone does not establish which interval must win; timing terms can change the path score.
4. Wait for the applicable stability policy, then publish an event if accepted.
ILLUSTRATIVE OUTPUT TO H6: one HELLO gloss with score/start/end/commit time. If the system nevertheless emits duplicates, that is a sequence error, not proof of multiple real signs.
H.source: Toy probabilities and assumed successful acceptance; runtime mechanism: LiveSegmental.decode and commitment logic in LiveReelDecoder.swift. General correspondence: H4/H5 ↔ R4/R5.

H.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: committed HELLO and its score from H5; the paper T5 model/token map from E8/D5.
CONDITIONAL EXAMPLE: if this accepted score is≥0.60, the retained T5 interface encodes “hi hello”.
1. Bundled token map gives hi→7102 and hello→21820. These two IDs are verified metadata, not invented scores.
2. Append EOS and pad to 64; mask real tokens versus padding. Encoder hidden output is[1,64,256].
3. Begin decoding with the configured decoder-start token; append the model's next token until EOS or length limit. Runtime has no reference English sentence.
4. On Finish, flush pending recognition, finalize English, display and use local speech.
ILLUSTRATIVE OUTPUT: a greeting such as “Hello.” The exact text and score are not claimed as a measured replay.
H.source: Verified token IDs: Models/stage3_tokens.json word_ids.hi/hello. Runtime template: LiveReelStage3.swift:bucket and generateUnpooled. This is the paper T5 path.

I.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: admitted isolated clips, fixed class map and preserved signer/recording memberships from I1/I2.
1. Prepare training and validation separately. Validation is not a source of optimizer gradients; protected test data is not used for development selection.
2. Balanced class sampling gives each class comparable expected exposure. For n_c examples in class c, inverse-frequency clip weights make total class mass comparable. Replacement allows repeats and omissions within an epoch; it does not mean every clip is seen exactly once.
3. Training augmentation varies geometry/time; mirrored landmarks require both an X reflection and anatomical hand-slot exchange. Exact transforms are stage-specific.
4. Produce inputs with batch dimension B: [B,32,61,5], [B,16,3,512], valid[B,16,3], boxes[B,16,3,4], target[B].
OUTPUT TO I4: training batches and a separately prepared fixed validation view. Sampling frequency is different from class-weighted loss.
I.source: Source supplement: train_stage_1_v17.py:mirror_v17, augmentation and sampler. Multimodal input contracts: LiveReelModels.swift. Paper training controls: pp. 76–78.

I.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: branch tensors and target class IDs from I3.
1. Forward calculation produces 100 logits. Conceptually p_k=exp(l_k)/Σexp(l_j); numerical cross-entropy works from logits using log-softmax.
2. Base label smoothing uses y=(1−ε)onehot+ε/K, K=100, ε=0.1. Thus target class mass 0.901 and each other class 0.001 under the uniform-all-classes convention.
3. Loss L=−Σy_k log p_k, averaged over the batch. A correct top-1 prediction can still receive loss depending on its distribution.
4. Backpropagation applies the chain rule: ∂L/∂w=(∂L/∂z)(∂z/∂w), composed through the actual network.
5. Optimizer uses those gradients to adjust trainable parameters after the batch. Frozen parameters have no optimizer update.
OUTPUT: new parameters for the next forward pass, not a model that relearns during ordinary inference.
I.source: Source supplement: base label_smoothing provenance; train_stage_1_v17.py training loop. General cross-entropy/chain-rule explanation; no new measured result.

I.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: I6 gradients and current parameters; validation features remain from I2/I3.
AdamW schematic update: w←(1−ηλ)w−η·m̂/(√v̂+ε). m̂/v̂ are bias-corrected moving summaries of gradients; η is learning rate, λ weight decay. This is more than directly subtracting the scalar loss.
BASE RECORD: peak LR3×10⁻⁴, warm-up 8 epochs, then cosine scheduling; selected base epoch 100 from 130 recorded epochs (paper 96.83% base validation).
LATER REPLAY: peak 5×10⁻⁵, warm-up 4, mild roll±12° in run_v2. It is a later stage with different objective/data.
EMA, when enabled: w_ema←d·w_ema+(1−d)·w_current; recorded replay d=0.999. EMA is a separate averaged copy, not a cap on gradient updates.
OUTPUT: selected branch checkpoints; I8 fusion trains a gated correction from the branch embeddings/scores, then supplies P1.
I.source: Recorded base LR trace: stage1-architecture log2026-10-19; run_v2 recipe; checkpoint lineage report 20261013. Paper base result/epoch numbers: pp. 93–94.

P.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: P1 weights from I8; P2 approved phrase recordings with sign start/end/gloss annotations.
1. Use one annotated sign segment per recognition example rather than assigning one class to an entire multi-sign phrase.
2. Construct allowed views of that segment; normalize/resample landmarks and select corresponding cached hand times using the same interval.
3. Run the landmark and hand encoders from P1. Frozen means their weights do not change, while their forward calculations still run.
CACHED OUTPUT PER EXAMPLE TO P5: landmark embedding[256], hand embedding[256], landmark logits[100], hand logits[100], plus target class and source identity.
This cache is what lets head adaptation reuse branch representations without recomputing gradients through both encoders.
P.source: Source supplement: train_unified_phrase_adapt_v17.py cached feature preparation and requires_grad flags; selected phrase metadata. Paper: p.79.

P.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: P4 phrase feature rows, I3/I8 isolated replay features and a frozen starting reference head.
1. New fusion head gives logits for every mixed batch row.
2. Hard class CE supervises the labeled sign.
3. The configured pair term focuses on the specified confusable pair using eligible rows.
4. Replay source rows compare the new head with the starting reference distribution: KL at temperature 2, scaled by 4.
5. Anchor penalty averages squared differences between trainable head parameters and their starting values.
COMBINATION: L = CE+λ_pair L_pair+λ_retain L_KL+λ_anchor L_anchor. Coefficients must come from this phase's actual recipe; do not copy a later phase's settings backward.
OUTPUT TO P6: one scalar loss. Replay still matters because the head's mapping can change while the encoders remain frozen.
P.source: Source supplement: train_unified_phrase_adapt_v17.py:348–377, source masks and anchor initialization. Exact selected-phase values are distinguished from trainer defaults.

P.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: P.b combined loss and the trainable fusion head.
1. zero_grad clears previous batch gradients.
2. backward calculates head gradients.
3. Clip the head's total gradient norm to 1.
4. AdamW updates the head; cosine scheduling changes its learning rate over the run.
5. Evaluate phrase and isolated validation features without parameter updates; apply the recorded selection/retention rule.
UNCHANGED: landmark encoder and hand temporal encoder weights. TRAINABLE: fusion head parameters; they can change overall class decisions.
SAVED PHASE: selected epoch 21; its recorded current LR is not automatically the initial LR.
OUTPUT P8→C1: phrase-adapted model. This is still word classification, not English generation or boundary training.
P.source: Source supplement: train_unified_phrase_adapt_v17.py:313–318,379–382 and selected run_v2 phrase metadata. Paper training sequence: p.79.

C.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: P8 parent weights, admitted phrase candidate intervals and earlier isolated examples from I3.
Start by copying reference predictions/parameters from the parent. Draw the mixed interval/replay batch.
FULL replay: retain its label and allow reference-distribution retention.
PARTIAL replay: shorten the sign and keep its parent label; exclude whole-clip reference retention because that reference saw a different view.
TINY replay: replace an eligible non-partial row with a short fragment and use a flat 100-class target.
RECORDED SETTINGS: partial probability 0.30 with minimum retained fraction 0.25; rejection probability 0.15 on eligible non-partial replay, fragment fraction 0.10–0.25.
OUTPUT TO C5: logits, class targets and explicit partial/rejection/replay masks. Those probabilities are conditional pipeline choices, not independent percentages of the entire corpus.
C.source: Source supplement: train_span_recognizer_v17.py:fragment construction and row masks; selected run_frag25_reject invocation. No data or training gate was changed.

C.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: C.a batch logits/masks; frozen parent logits on eligible full replay; starting trainable parameters.
1. L_class=CE on non-rejection rows.
2. L_flat=−mean_k log p_k on tiny-fragment rows; weight 0.5. Uniform mass over 100 classes discourages a concentrated guess without adding a 101 st word.
3. L_retain=4·KL(p_ref,T=2 || p_current,T=2), full eligible replay only.
4. L_anchor=Σ mean((w−w_start)²), weight 0.01.
5. Add applicable terms: L=L_class+0.5 L_flat+L_retain+0.01 L_anchor. Each term's own row averaging matters; an absent group contributes zero.
OUTPUT TO C6: scalar loss. Label smoothing, flat-fragment supervision and reference retention have different targets and eligibility even though each uses distributions.
C.source: Source supplement: train_span_recognizer_v17.py:344–366. Exact coefficients and masks come from that implementation plus selected invocation; they are not paper-reported ablation results.

C.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: C.b loss gradients.
SELECTED PRIMARY: encoders trainable at LR1×10⁻⁵, fusion head LR2×10⁻⁵; AdamW decay 0.001, cosine scheduling, global gradient clipping 1. Both parameter groups learn; they do not use the same step scale.
TOY clipping, separate from ATLAS measurements: g=(3,4), norm=5; with cap 1, multiply by 1/5 →(0.6,0.8). In general g←g·min(1,c/(||g||+ε)). This bounds the gradient norm, not the exact AdamW parameter-update norm.
SELECTION: lowest development WER subject to isolated floors; chosen primary epoch 4 of 8 planned.
SCOPED REFINEMENT: separate reviewed transition views adapt fusion with frozen encoders; preserve original primary scores and use adapted evidence conditionally.
OUTPUT TO D1/R4: retained primary plus guarded refinement evidence.
C.source: Source supplement: train_span_recognizer_v17.py parameter groups/selection; run_frag25_reject; confidence refinement recipe. Toy norm arithmetic is illustrative.

B.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: the same admitted video identity with teacher MediaPipe pose outputs and student Apple observations.
1. Read cached teacher sign-timing outputs; derive normalized O/B/I distributions. This teacher was pretrained on German Sign Language but provides timing, not ASL word labels.
2. Student raw observations have their actual timestamps t.
3. Map each t to teacher index round(t·teacher_grid_FPS), clip to valid index range, and select that target distribution.
OUTPUT TO B5: aligned q=[q_O,q_B,q_I] paired with each student feature observation.
The teacher is frozen: it supplies numerical supervision without receiving optimizer updates. Matching timestamped views is essential; the two landmark pipelines are not assumed to have identical coordinates.
B.source: Source supplement: train_av_boundary_v17.py:teacher_obi,student_inputs,aligned. Excluded memberships are enforced by that trainer. Paper teacher/student description: pp. 78–79.

B.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: Apple raw observations/timestamps from B1 and aligned targets q from B3.
Features 450=122 normalized XY+122 time-normalized XY differences+61 presence+61 confidence+84 hand-local XY.
Build windows[B,64,450] and valid[B,64]. Project 450→256, add learned positions, then four Transformer layers (eight heads, feed-forward width 512). Normalize the read-position representation; linear head 256→3.
For lookahead 6, read index=64−1−6=57: six later window positions inform this estimate. Padding is masked.
LOSS STEPS: logits→log-softmax→L=−mean_i Σ_k q_ik log p_ik. Target uncertainty is preserved instead of forcing every frame to a hard one-hot teacher guess.
OUTPUT TO B6: mean soft-target cross-entropy for student parameters.
B.source: Source supplement: temporal_boundary_v17.py features; av_boundary_v17.py:windows/AVBoundary.forward; train_av_boundary_v17.py:training loss.

B.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: B5 student loss and separate held-out-video teacher/student pairs.
UPDATE: clear gradients→backpropagate student→clip norm→AdamW step→OneCycle schedule. Exact selected command overrides must be checked before calling a class default the recorded LR.
VALIDATION: KL(q||p)=Σq log(q/p) measures timing-distribution agreement. The compatible trainer keeps minimum held-out KL. Cross-entropy and KL differ by target entropy, so neither number is vocabulary accuracy.
OUTPUT B8→D1: selected student weights/config. Runtime R3 uses Apple-derived features,64 positions and six-position lookahead. The large offline teacher is not run for each phone frame.
At a nominal 20 Hz,6/20=0.30 s accounts for lookahead alone; decoder and language waiting are separate.
B.source: Source supplement: train_av_boundary_v17.py:267–296; av_boundary_v17.py; LiveReelModels.swift:97–190. Paper: timing component roles, pp. 78–82.

E.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: E1 gloss–English pairs and their train/validation memberships.
1. Encode confidence bucket before each gloss: hi≥0.60, mid≥0.40, otherwise lo.
2. Tokenize this evidence string into source IDs and attention mask. Tokenize the target English rendering separately.
3. Pad source with the tokenizer pad ID, source mask 0; pad labels with −100 so those positions are ignored by the loss.
4. Choose the smallest recorded bucket L∈{24,40,64} fitting both source and target; the matching trainer refuses truncation.
OUTPUT TO E3/E4: source IDs[B,L], mask[B,L], target IDs[B,L]. Confidence is source evidence, not the target sentence.
The corpus's held-out evaluation sessions are excluded from training; synthetic/text supervision quality still needs evaluation.
E.source: Recorded recipe and source supplement: train_stage3_multisentence_v17.py:tensors/batches; stage3_multisentence_bakeoff_v17_20260929/tiny/recipe.json. Paper English path only.

E.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: E2 token tensors and pretrained T5-efficient-tiny initialization.
ENCODER: source token embeddings→four encoder layers→hidden states[B,L,256].
DECODER TRAINING: shift target IDs right and insert decoder-start token. Causal self-attention uses only earlier target positions; cross-attention reads encoder states. Four decoder layers produce vocabulary logits[B,L,V].
TOKEN LOSS: for each non-padding target position, compare logits with the correct token using cross-entropy, then average according to the model's masked loss.
BACKPROP: chain this scalar loss through decoder and encoder trainable weights.
OUTPUT TO E6: gradients. At runtime, the prefix consists of generated tokens rather than supplied correct target tokens; training teacher forcing does not give the app the answer.
E.source: Verified T5 config: d_model 256, encoder layers 4, decoder layers 4, heads 4. Source: train_stage3_multisentence_v17.py labels=model loss; export_stage3_t5_coreml_v17.py. Paper model≈15.6M parameters.

E.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: E5 token-loss gradients and the recorded T5 recipe.
1. Clip gradient norm to 1 and update with Adafactor; batch 32, peak LR3×10⁻⁴, FP32.
2. Learning-rate warm-up lasts 100 optimizer steps; the recorded schedule decays linearly toward 10% over the bounded run's step budget.
3. Keep the final step of this recorded run. Validation is measured separately, not used to choose the best epoch.
PAPER RECEIPT: optimizer step 4,539, validation loss 0.2515. This is token prediction loss, not percent translation accuracy.
EXPORT: source IDs/mask[1,64]→encoder hidden[1,64,256]. Decoder takes prefix IDs[1,64], source hidden/mask and position[1], returning next token. Stop at EOS/limit, then detokenize.
OUTPUT TO R6 via D: one English model in two runtime graphs.
E.source: Matched recipe.json and targeted training_result.history[-1] at stage3_multisentence_bakeoff_v17_20260929/tiny; paper English validation result. Export contracts: export_stage3_t5_coreml_v17.py.

D.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: C8 primary/refined recognizer, B8 student, E8 paper T5 and pretrained crop encoder, plus label/token maps.
Pin identities before conversion. The recognizer package contains landmark/hand temporal branches and fusion; it does not absorb every pipeline component.
VISUAL INTERFACES: crop image 256×256→512 features; recognizer inputs[8,32,61,5],[8,16,3,512],[8,16,3],[8,16,3,4]→word logits[8,100]. Short batches repeat the final input into unused slots and discard corresponding extra outputs.
TIMING: [1,64,450] +valid[1,64]→[1,3].
PAPER ENGLISH: [1,64] source IDs/mask→hidden[1,64,256], then repeated decoder steps.
PRECISION: selected visual exports FP16; retained paper-English exports FP32. Conversion targets the runtime; it does not train a new model.
D.source: Source supplement: export_dual_confidence.py; LiveReelModels.swift; export_stage3_t5_coreml_v17.py. The English interface follows the paper-scoped T5 component.

D.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: pinned source checkpoint and D3 converted graph, tested on identical prepared inputs.
1. Match input ordering, dtype, shapes, masks and label map before comparing results.
2. Inspect logits/scores and per-example top predictions. Equal aggregate accuracy can hide different individual predictions.
3. Assess the appropriate task contract: recognition, timing or English. A conversion comparison is not a new independent generalization study.
4. Bundle verified model graphs with tokenizer/label maps and the selected runtime settings. Decoder thresholds and repairs belong to application logic/configuration, not a learned segmental-model weight file.
OUTPUT TO D6: compatible packaged components and their verification evidence. Source-package bytes, compiled bytes and app download size are different quantities.
D.source: Source supplement: model export wrappers and mobile interfaces; measured-release inventory report 2026-10-19. No new export, benchmark, build or test-gate evaluation was run for this board.

D.body:
INPUT ORIGIN: D5 model assets/configuration.
LOAD/WARM: initialize inference interfaces and perform warm-up calls before live processing to reduce first-call planning overhead.
ENGINE QUEUE: frame processing and cached evidence→boundary timing→candidate scoring→stable gloss events. R2 evidence is reused by R3 and R4; R3 timing is reused by R4 and R5.
PAPER ENGLISH QUEUE: committed glosses feed R6; Finish flushes pending recognition before final English. MAIN THREAD: render text and trigger local speech.
MEASURE SEPARATELY: model storage, peak runtime RAM, compute latency, sustained thermal behavior, recognition quality and sequence/translation quality.
The paper's 31.14 ms extraction-to-recognizer measurement excludes parts of camera-to-speech delay. Inference keeps learned parameters fixed.
D.source: Source supplement: LiveReelApp.swift/LiveReelViewController.swift queues and model warmup; retained T5 interface. Paper prototype and performance sections; English scoped to paper T5.
